evidence.testTitle: MSG-013: IRC +ircord/edit cross-author edit has no persistent or recipient effects
evidence.scenarioScope: Alice can edit her own message when editing is permitted.
assertionDetails: IRC +ircord/edit targets cross-author; all three aliases are executed separately through IRC PRIVMSG and REST POST tags, using real members and a foreign secret-channel row.

evidence.testTitle: message denial boundaries MSG-007: cross-author edit is rejected without mutation or delivery

SQLite retains all three original unredacted rows; separate recreated Miniflare runtime independently reads both histories with unrelated content preserved.

assertionDetails: All users and rootadmin are provisioned through genuine public registration/bootstrap/login on the frozen production runtime with unique passwords; original credentials and SQLite directory are reused by a copied-bundle Miniflare fixture.

The fixture subclasses only SessionDO.invalidateAccountPermissions to return 0, modeling lost eager invalidation delivery after Accounts committed disable; no authentication, dispatch, ingress, outbound permission checks, account storage or WebSocket attachment is overridden or fabricated.

Two independently authenticated Bob IRC sessions successfully publish/receive before disable, actual Bob event stream receives the control, Charlie admin disable is exactly 403, and genuine root disable is exactly 200 with ok=true and invalidatedSessions=0.

Both original Bob sockets are unconditionally asserted OPEN after committed disable; the original sender unconditionally sends PRIVMSG disabled-surviving-socket-publish and the unchanged production ingress check closes it with code 1000/reason Account no longer available.

Existing Bob REST append is exactly 401; Alice private post still reaches authorized IRC/event recipients, while Bob receiver/event stream and unrelated Charlie IRC/event stream receive no private content and no stream receives forbidden publish content.

A second device can remain open after account-wide membership cleanup; if still OPEN its next PING triggers the unchanged credential recheck and closure, rather than assuming membership removal always immediately closes every socket.

After actual fixture disposal, SQLite contains no disabled IRC/REST publish, retains original/unrelated/Alice-new message authors and bodies, stores Bob disabled_at with Alice enabled, preserves root admin role and empty Bob/custom-channel role assignments; a new uninstrumented production runtime keeps Bob REST at 401 and retains legitimate/unrelated history.

assertionDetails: After a live positive marker, the real WebSocket/TCP reader is paused and 12 private REST messages are published with matching saved IDs and content; an independent authorized IRC/event recipient progresses while outsider Dave sees no private bodies.

assertionDetails: Real authenticated members upload524305 bytes in unmoderated channel; +m denies ordinary member on current/legacy aliases before grant; attach_files-only grant permits both aliases, while other channel upload, text POST400 and q-role creation403 remain denied.

Denied attempts preserve exact media metadata/chunks/quota/object and selected channel domain; three actual IRC/event witnesses receive barriers only; member download stays200 after grant removal and secret outsider GET404.

Exact owner/provider/scope/ready metadata, SQLite SHA and two chunks or R2 object size, quota increments and full-byte reads are asserted; grant succeeds after recreation, removal denies both aliases after another recreation; independent resource bytes stay healthy; voice/op positive controls work.

R2 bucket operations use the persisted media_uploads.object_key (with ID fallback where the test helper explicitly provides it), while public URLs use the media ID; the two identifiers are not assumed equal.

R2 bucket operations use the persisted media_uploads.object_key (with ID fallback where the test helper explicitly provides it), while public URLs use the media ID; the two identifiers are not assumed equal.

evidence.scenarioScope: File-size limits are enforced.
assertionDetails: Real10MiB+1 upload413; ten10MiB accepted; over100MiB403; delete releases capacity, alias overage403, independent Bob bytes and bucket object count preserved.
After actual complete R2/SQLite recreation and fresh logins, quota403 and removed-object404 remain, Bob bytes and remaining bucket metadata match.

evidence.testTitle: r2 10485760 byte real upload limits MEDIA-009 MEDIA-012 ABUSE-007: oversized and exhausted quota denials are silent and inert across restart
evidence.scenarioScope: R2 upload size and full 100 MiB quota with actual 10 MiB objects, observed denial windows and restart.
assertionDetails: Independent Alice, Bob and Charlie authenticate via public registration, login and IRC PASS; Alice and Bob join a secret channel and Charlie is outside it. R2 stores real upload bytes in workerd persistence.

Both upload aliases reject actual 10 MiB+1 request bodies with 413 and no Location, content or UUID; filling exactly 100 MiB with 10 MiB objects succeeds, and both aliases reject further payloads with 403 without Location, payload or UUID.
